conventions.convention: Geometric intersection orders the tangent blocks A first, B second; interchanging them multiplies the integral count by (−1)^(ab).
Normal orientation is tangent-first. With cohomology-first, front-evaluation cap, a normal Thom extension satisfies ᾱ cap [M]=(−1)^(rz)i_*[Z]. Coefficients are Z or F₂.

Numerical self-intersection requires compact boundaryless A in boundaryless M, with 2 dim A=dim M. M need not be compact. Tubular charts have identity normal differential, and push-offs inherit A's orientation.
The diagonal normal identification is (v,w)↦w−v, orientation-preserving for tangent-first normal orientation and the transported diagonal orientation.
Θ_n and bP_(n+1) are defined here for n≥5 under countable choice, using oriented h-cobordism classes. Parallelizable fillings mean actually trivial tangent bundles, not merely stably trivial ones.

Quaternionic fibres have basis (1,i,j,k); clutching is upper-to-lower (a,v)_+∼(a,a^h v a^j)_−. The lower coordinate disk is positively oriented in S⁴, the upper one negatively oriented; both basic multiplication clutchings have Euler number +1.
W_(h,j) has base-then-fibre orientation, and M_(h,j)=∂W_(h,j) has outward-normal-first boundary orientation.
The boundary middle form is defined on im(H⁴(W,∂W;R)→H⁴(W;R)) using relative lifts and the relative fundamental class; it is not the closed-manifold form applied to W.

The filling candidate requires integral H³(M)=H⁴(M)=0 and a supplied oriented filling. Its relative p₁ lift is unique; q is an integral relative square, and λ=2q−σ modulo 7. No general filling-existence assertion is made.
Compact smooth finite-CW models are proved under countable choice; general Thom, characteristic-class, duality, Gysin and signature uses retain full AC.
Copowers exist objectwise from finite biproducts; a functorial copower assignment requires a supplied family of representing objects and universal elements.
Module notation uses finite-dimensional left modules over supplied model algebras and chosen small representatives; a kernel from A to B is a finite k-linear (B,A)-bimodule.
The Lex inverse is the coend of ā⊠F(a); the Rex inverse is the end of ā⊠G(a). For the identity these give A* and A respectively.
Nʳ=ΦʳΨˡ(identity) and Nˡ=ΦˡΨʳ(identity); in the model they are A*⊗_A− and Hom_A(A*,−). Their adjunction is Nʳ⊣Nˡ; neither is asserted to be an equivalence generally.

load_bearing.statement: Assume AC. For a smooth R-oriented rank-r real bundle over a closed R-oriented smooth n-manifold, R=Z or F₂, a transverse section has tangent-first oriented zero locus Z with normal bundle E|Z, and e(E) cap [M]=(−1)^(r(n−r))i_*[Z]. When r=n, Euler evaluation is the signed zero count.

Assume AC. For compact boundaryless oriented Aᵃ embedded in oriented boundaryless Mⁿ with 2a=n and tangent-first oriented normal bundle, A·A=⟨e(ν_A),[A]⟩. The value is independent of normalized tube and transverse push-off. A rank-r oriented bundle over a closed oriented r-manifold has signed transverse zero count equal to its Euler evaluation.

For finite k-linear abelian categories with supplied small module models, Φˡ(M)=Hom_A(M*,−) and Φʳ(M)=M⊗_A− give equivalences Lex(A,B)≃Aᵒᵖ⊠B≃Rex(A,B). On ā⊠b they are Hom_A(a,X)⊗_k b and Hom_A(X,a)*⊗_k b. The Deligne product uses its existence theorem's AC assumption.

Assume AC. For closed R-oriented smooth Mⁿ and closed R-oriented embedded Zᶻ, R=Z or F₂, the tangent-first normal Thom extension α has absolute image ᾱ satisfying ᾱ cap [M]=(−1)^((n−z)z)i_*[Z], using an identity-normal-differential tubular chart.

Assume AC. For complementary-dimensional closed oriented embedded A,B in closed oriented smooth M, I(A,B)=⟨PD[A] cup PD[B],[M]⟩ in the cohomology-first cap convention. Nontransverse intersections use transverse maps on the original source. The mod-two formula needs no orientations; the number depends only on represented homology classes.

Assume AC. For finite-dimensional unital k-algebras R,S, (R⊗_k S)-mod with (X,Y)↦X⊗_kY is a finite Deligne product: restriction gives the stated equivalence for every k-linear abelian target E. Supplied module models transport this to abstract finite categories.

Assume AC. Q_W is well defined, symmetric and nondegenerate on its image I. If oriented eight-dimensional fillings W,W′ have identified oriented boundary M with integral H³(M)=H⁴(M)=0, then σ(W∪_M(−W′))=σ(W)−σ(W′).
Assume AC. For a closed oriented smooth seven-manifold M with integral H³(M)=H⁴(M)=0 and supplied oriented eight-dimensional fillings W,W′, N=W∪_M(−W′) satisfies ⟨p₁(TN)²,[N]⟩=q(W)−q(W′).

Assume AC. If closed oriented smooth M⁷ has integral H³(M)=H⁴(M)=0 and at least one supplied oriented compact smooth filling, λ(M)=2q(W)−σ(W) modulo 7 is filling-independent, preserved by orientation-preserving boundary diffeomorphisms and negated by orientation reversal. No universal filling existence is asserted.
Assume AC. In the fixed quaternionic and clutching orientations, e(ξ_(h,j))=(h+j)u and p₁(ξ_(h,j))=2(h−j)u.

In supplied finite module models, the Lex kernel coend has universal cowedge ρ_a(f⊗λ)=λ∘f into M≅M**; the Rex kernel end has universal wedge ω_a(m)(x)=m⊗x. These kernels are functorial and give quasi-inverses to Φˡ and Φʳ, without assuming unrestricted completeness.

With a chosen finite module model, Nʳ≅A*⊗_A− and Nˡ≅Hom_A(A*,−), with explicit adjunction Nʳ⊣Nˡ. Their intrinsic formulas are the coend Hom(X,a)*⊗a and the end Hom(a,X)⊗a, and they are independent of module model up to canonical compatible natural isomorphism.

concerns.concern: Unresolved size/choice gap in Statement (ii) and Proof 4.1. The target E is an arbitrary k-linear abelian category, possibly a proper definable class under rem-category-theory-class-and-size-conventions. The determination lemma chooses cokernels for one H over its set-sized source. Proof 4.1 then says that fixing source presentations makes H↦H̄ a functor over all H, but has not supplied simultaneous biproduct/cokernel choices over this potentially proper class. Ordinary AC selects set-indexed data, not class-indexed data; full faithfulness plus objectwise essential surjectivity does not supply the specified quasi-inverse. The concrete finite-module formulas remain sound. [Milne, Tannakian Categories](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/tcdraft.pdf), printed pp. 95–98, footnote 4 and Proposition 10.6 proof, explicitly restricts targets to small categories for this construction. Step 7 should establish the stronger class-sized assertion or identify the missing target-size/universal-data hypothesis.

Proof 3.1 states that object-variable transformations compose as g↦g∘h∘h′. With h:Y→Y′ as fixed in Step 2.2 and h′:Y′→Y″, the correctly typed precomposition is g↦g∘h′∘h. The displayed order is reversed. The supplied representing-data hypothesis and the functoriality argument otherwise close immediately.

seams_checked.note: The lambda proof cites the closed eight-dimensional formula 45σ=7p₂−p₁² with AC. Boundary fillings are handled by separately proved relative forms and gluing, not by applying the closed formula directly to a filling.

Consumers supply connected compact h-cobordisms with closed simply connected faces and total dimension at least six. Θ_n uses n≥5; the two-disk complement in a d-sphere uses d≥6. Relative product and countable-choice qualifications are retained.

Euler clutching calibration uses the Gauss-degree lemma's general nonzero-boundary clause on D⁴ and the determinant formula for nondegenerate zeros. It does not assume its coordinate field points outward.

Module-model uses retain supplied splitting data or explicitly select a set-indexed splitting under AC. Rex and Lex classifications retain finite-dimensionality, supplied small module sources, commuting actions and agreeing k-scalars. The owned large-target concern is separate from citation fidelity.

The page declares this prerequisite, but its listed A/B items contain no direct citation to an owned intersection item. Current page prose asserts no stronger intersection proposition; the edge is contextual rather than an identified item-level use.

Graph/diagonal consumers preserve the ordered intersection convention. The twisted diagonal proof applies the normal-Thom supplier on an oriented cover, explicitly extends integral coefficients to Q, and accounts for both the first-minus-second normal sign and the cap shuffle.

The surgery remark and companion counterexamples use compact closed representatives. The diagonal obstruction retains ν_Δ≅TS², Euler evaluation and AC; the middle-surgery example uses the cup/intersection theorem on actual factor spheres before extending bilinearly.

def-middle-dimensional-intersection-form states Q_M(PD[A],PD[B])=I(A,B) only for closed oriented embedded complementary representatives, with the cohomology-first cap convention, ordered factors and inherited AC.

The embedded statement retains closed oriented representatives and even middle dimension, so the zero-locus shuffle is +1. The immersion push-off lemma invokes the bundle zero-count clause over its closed source and proves the separate double-point contribution locally.

The zero-section/graph index item repeats the horizontal-then-vertical block determinant calculation rather than applying a small-push-off theorem to an unrestricted field. The Euler-characteristic corollary retains closedness, AC, admissible bundle hypotheses and the diagonal/mod-two clauses.
